title: Omnichannel support for B2B: best practices and tools | Pylon
summary: Pylon's guide to omnichannel B2B support: run email, Slack, Teams, WhatsApp, Telegram, and Discord in one queue, with a sourced tool comparison.
body_markdown:
**Short answer:** B2B teams manage email, Slack, and Microsoft Teams together by bringing every channel into one queue, where each message becomes an issue linked to the customer's account, with one set of SLAs, routing rules, and reporting. The best setups add the chat apps customers already use, like WhatsApp, Telegram, and Discord, without asking anyone to switch. Pylon does this natively, with Slack, email, chat, Discord, WhatsApp, Telegram, and SMS on every plan, and Microsoft Teams and Google Chat on Advanced and Enterprise.


## What is omnichannel support?


Omnichannel support means customers can reach you on any channel and your team works every conversation in one place, with the full account history in view. Multichannel support just means you offer several channels; each one can still be a separate inbox with separate context.


The difference shows up when a customer emails on Monday and follows up in a shared Slack channel on Wednesday. In an omnichannel setup, both land on the same account, with the same SLA clock, and whoever picks it up sees both.


## How do B2B teams manage email, Slack, and Teams in one queue?


They connect each channel to one help desk, link each channel or chat to a customer account, and let routing and SLAs work the same way no matter where a message started. In Pylon, a message in a connected channel creates an issue, and replies sync back to where the customer wrote.


A few practices that make it work:


- **Link channels to accounts.** A shared Slack channel, a Teams chat, or a WhatsApp group should map to one account so context follows the customer.
- **Use one SLA policy per tier, not per channel.** Customers on the same plan should get the same response time whether they emailed or posted in Slack.
- **Route on account and skill, not just channel.** (In Pylon, skill-based routing is on Advanced and Enterprise.) Send issues to the people who know the product area or own the account.
- **Thread ongoing chats.** Teams chats, WhatsApp, Telegram, and SMS don't have separate threads per request. Pylon's issue conversation view (on by default) uses AI to add each new message to the right open issue, or creates a new one when the topic changes.
- **Keep one knowledge base behind every channel** so answers match everywhere.


More on the Slack side:[Slack-first support for B2B teams](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/slack-first-b2b-support) and[Microsoft Teams customer support](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/microsoft-teams-customer-support-2026) .

## What support software handles WhatsApp, Telegram, and Discord groups?


Pylon supports WhatsApp, Telegram, and Discord natively on every plan, including group chats, with messages, files, and reactions synced both ways. Each conversation becomes an issue you can route, track against SLAs, and report on like any other channel.


- **WhatsApp:** connect group chats through Pylon's WhatsApp business account using the group's invite link, or connect your own WhatsApp Business number through Meta. Both 1:1 chats and group chats create issues. ([Pylon docs](https://docs.usepylon.com/pylon-docs/integrations/chat/whatsapp) )
- **Telegram:** make one org-level connection, then each teammate connects a personal Telegram account. Link Telegram chats to accounts, and new messages in linked chats create issues. ([Pylon docs](https://docs.usepylon.com/pylon-docs/integrations/chat/telegram) )
- **Discord:** new posts in forum channels create issues automatically. In regular channels, either every message becomes an issue or users react with the ticket emoji to open one. ([Pylon docs](https://docs.usepylon.com/pylon-docs/integrations/chat/discord) )


For how real teams run these channels, see[how Privy and Alchemy scale support on Telegram and Discord](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/how-to-scale-support-telegram-discord-from-privy-alchemy) and[Discord customer support](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/discord-customer-support-2026) .


Other tools cover some of these channels. Help Scout lists WhatsApp, Instagram, and Messenger on its Standard plan, Front lists WhatsApp on Professional and Enterprise, and Fin lists WhatsApp among its channels. Intercom supports Discord natively ([Intercom help: Connect your Discord channel](https://www.intercom.com/help/en/articles/14136689-connect-your-discord-channel) ).


## What features matter in an omnichannel support platform?


1. **One queue for every channel,** with each issue tied to an account.
2. **Routing and SLAs** that work across channels.
3. **Agents that work every channel.** In Pylon, Support Agent answers using your content and hands off by your escalation rules, and Slack Agent works from Slack with the same context.
4. **A knowledge base** that feeds both customers and agents.
5. **Reporting by channel, account, and team.**
6. **Integrations** with your CRM, issue tracker, and call recorder so context travels with the issue.

## How do you roll out omnichannel support?


A typical rollout, in our experience, goes in 4 steps:


1. **Audit:** list every channel customers use today and the volume on each.
2. **Configure:** connect channels, link them to accounts, and set SLAs and routing.
3. **Soft launch:** move a few accounts or one channel first, and check routing and threading.
4. **Expand and measure:** add the rest, and track first response time, SLA attainment, and CSAT by channel.


## FAQ


**How do B2B teams manage email, Slack, and Teams together?**


They bring every channel into one queue, link each channel to a customer account, and run one set of SLAs, routing rules, and reporting across all of them.


**What support software handles WhatsApp and Telegram groups?**


Pylon supports WhatsApp and Telegram group chats natively on every plan, with messages, files, and reactions synced both ways. Discord is also supported on every plan.


**What's the difference between omnichannel and multichannel support?**


Multichannel means you offer several channels. Omnichannel means every conversation lands in one place with the account history in view.
